coverage.found: Export permit needed for cocoa, coffee and rubber (tralac trade policy review, dated). Produce Monitoring Board does quality and support; Sierra Leone Produce Marketing Company has no monopoly. A national commodity board is planned (premiermedia-sl.com ?p=27485). No current register or periodic report found. Nothing buildable yet.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Search returned no Sierra Leone co-operative law material (registrar, annual return or audit duty unverified). BSL supervises community banks and Financial Services Associations under the Other Financial Services Act (2016 figures: 17 community banks, 51 FSAs, 10 credit-only MFIs). Candidate C08 (weak).

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: SLeSHI (social health insurance) is still in preparation per 2022 stakeholder reports; no provider accreditation or claims process found. Private-insurer billing market looks thin. Candidate C09 (unverified).

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03. Pharmacy Board (PBSL) works under the Pharmacy and Drugs Act 2001; no 2026 renewal cycle found. The EPA Ozone Depleting Substances Regulations 2025 and Lead in Paint Regulations 2025 are covered under candidate C05.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security firms need an Office of National Security licence under the National Security and Central Intelligence Act 2023; ONS named 46 unlicensed agencies (awokonewspapersl.com ?p=118194). No cleaning or manpower agency regime found. Candidate C04.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Sierra Leone Local Content Agency Act 2016 requires an annual Sierra Leonean Content Plan; in March 2023 the Agency named 16 non-compliant firms, including hotels and a telecom operator. The Act was under review (2022/23 amendment). Filing deadline and supplier registration process not found. Candidate C03.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: No Sierra Leone-specific DNFBP list or FIU reporting guidance found. GIABA is running a capacity project covering Sierra Leone, and its real-estate-agent workshops (2024) covered Togo and The Gambia. Candidate C07 (unverified).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: National Tourist Board regulates tourist establishments; the licence, levy and grading rules were not found. The NRA's ECR duty explicitly covers hotels, guest houses, restaurants and bars, so the real compliance pain is C01.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Timber: seasonal logging and transport ban 1 June-31 October, CITES Afzelia (Lenge) log-movement certificates (Nov 2024), sole export agent Leadway, US$3,000 per container tax. Fish: Fisheries and Aquaculture Act 2018 requires vessel registration and licences for receiving, processing and marketing fish. Nothing found on EU catch certificates or cashew rules. Candidates C10 and C11.

coverage.category: 31. NRA electronic cash register (ECR) / Smart GST machine / e-invoicing regime (Finance Act 2020-2026)
coverage.found: GST-registered businesses must issue ECR-generated receipts (GST Act s.34, ECR Regulations 2021). The Finance Act 2026 s.21 inserted s.34(8): taxpayers must replace faulty ECRs at a gazetted cost, effective 1 Jan 2026. NRA began Smart GST machine distribution on 31 Aug 2026, targeting 10,000 businesses, and plans 5,000 replacement ECRs. The 2025 supplementary budget plans e-invoicing for building-materials and electronics sellers. Candidates C01 and C02.

coverage.category: 32. Environment Protection Agency Act 2022 licences and 2025 regulations (EIA licences, ODS, lead in paint)
coverage.found: EPA Act 2022 (Act 15) replaced the 2008 Act. In 2025 the EPA ran 1,184 inspections, approved 83 EIA licences and suspended Bennimix (a food producer) for lacking an EIA licence. ODS Regulations 2025 and Lead in Paint Regulations 2025 were enacted. Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 33. Fisheries and Aquaculture Act 2018: canoe registration, fish processors and marketers
coverage.found: Vessel registration certificate from the Director of Fisheries; Part X of the 1990 regulations, with a 2017 fee regulation, covers fish receiving, processing and marketing licences. Current fees and rules under the 2018 Act not verified. Candidate C10.

coverage.category: 34. Corporate Affairs Commission annual returns and beneficial ownership (Companies Act 2009)
coverage.found: The CAC is the registrar under the Companies Act 2009. A commercial guide says beneficial-ownership disclosure is a compliance duty, but no deadline, form or penalty was found. Candidate C07 (unverified).

coverage.category: 35. Bank of Sierra Leone: mobile money agents, community banks, Financial Services Associations
coverage.found: Mobile money guidelines 2015 (Other Financial Services Act 2001, Banking Act 2011); agents operate under regulated providers, so the buyer is the provider, not small agents. Candidate C08.

coverage.category: 36. Produce and commodity board reform (National Commodity Board, PMB, SLPMC)
coverage.found: Only press mentions of a planned National Commodity Board; no rules or registers found. Not reached beyond the one search because of budget.

coverage.category: 37. Private security licensing (ONS) - separate from category 26 manpower question
coverage.found: See category 26; the 2023 Act is the legal basis. Licence renewal terms and fees not found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Three searches (second-hand/pawn licence, police register, moneylender/BSL, Borrowers and Lenders Act) found no Sierra Leone second-hand dealer or pawnbroker licensing or police register regime; only foreign laws came back. Closest regimes: Moneylenders Act 1960 (Cap 240) licence requirement (Basma v Wanza, SC 2010, old.sierralii.org/node/298) and Borrowers and Lenders Act 2019 collateral registry for non-BSL lenders (parliament.gov.sl). Not confirmed whether pawn-type lending falls under either. No evidence of a dealer duty, so nothing buildable; one weak adjacent idea logged.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Two searches found no Sierra Leone beekeeper registration, hive registration, honey standard or export certification rule. Only donor/FAO apiculture projects (COOPI training, FAO-UN nutrition programme) and the general Standards Decree 1996 / SLSB. Nothing new; no registered duty. Not applicable as a software buyer.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Read full text of the Factories Act 1974 (FAOLEX copy). It requires factory registration (ss.6-9), notice of mechanical power and machinery installation (ss.10-11), return of machinery (s.12, form lists steam boilers and air/steam receivers with last thorough examination date), a general register (s.28), competent engineer in charge (ss.31-36), and 24-hour reporting of crane/hoist/receiver failures (s.45). No periodic boiler/lift/pressure-vessel certification or inspector-licensing regime found, and no subsidiary pressure-equipment rules. The Factory Inspectorate is under-equipped (2016 audit, Awoko). Very small market; nothing buildable.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Real regime found. SLEWRC Act 2011 (No. 13) replaced by SLEWRC Act 2025 (passed 24 July 2025, gazetted 14 July 2025, Part VII licensing incl. register; covers electricity, water and sanitation). Electricity and Water Licensing Rules SI 10/2019, Water Quality Supply Regulations SI 20/2019, and Bottled and Sachet Water Production Regulations SI 18/2019 (permits for producers and importers, source approval, record keeping, offences). 2016 order shutting 86 sachet water companies; later reporting that the SLSB certification list, SLEWRC register and Health Ministry verification did not match. Could not read the 2025 Act (parliament.gov.sl returned 503) so thresholds for small, community or independent water producers, fees and renewal cycle are unconfirmed. No sachet-water compliance software found. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 36. Produce and commodity board reform (National Commodity Board, PMB, SLPMC)
coverage.found: Premier Media (2 Feb 2026): after a Cabinet decision, a stakeholder meeting on 30 Jan 2026 chaired by the Chief Minister agreed to set up the Sierra Leone Commodity Board and make the government sole exporter of selected commodities, starting with cocoa. No licensing, registration, dates or other commodities stated. PMB regulates prices and quality (moisture meters, cutters). Older trade policy review: an export permit is required for cocoa, coffee and rubber; the SLPMC (2013) has no monopoly. Legal base is the 1949 Produce Marketing Ordinance (Cap 229); current licence rules, fees and forms not found. Private exporters use buying-agent networks with farmer traceability (Tradin, Kenema); cooperatives such as KayeiGworma pool exports. Impact of sole-exporter rule on agents and cooperatives is unknown. Candidate logged as unverified.
